work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. The Coast of Kent

content.text: Alarum. Fight at sea. Ordnance goes off. Enter a Lieutenant, Suffolk, disguised, a prisoner. The Master, a Master's Mate, Walter Whitmore, and prisoners.

lines.text: The gaudy, blabbing, and remorseful day
lines.plainText: The gaudy blabbing and remorseful day

lines.text: Is crept into the bosom of the sea;
lines.plainText: Is crept into the bosom of the sea

lines.text: And now loud-howling wolves arouse the jades
lines.plainText: And now loudhowling wolves arouse the jades

lines.text: That drag the tragic melancholy night,
lines.plainText: That drag the tragic melancholy night

lines.text: Who, with their drowsy, slow, and flagging wings
lines.plainText: Who with their drowsy slow and flagging wings

lines.text: Clip dead men's graves and from their misty jaws
lines.plainText: Clip dead men's graves and from their misty jaws

lines.text: Breathe foul contagious darkness in the air.
lines.plainText: Breathe foul contagious darkness in the air

lines.text: Therefore bring forth the soldiers of our prize;
lines.plainText: Therefore bring forth the soldiers of our prize

lines.text: For, whilst our pinnace anchors in the Downs,
lines.plainText: For whilst our pinnace anchors in the Downs

lines.text: Here shall they make their ransom on the sand,
lines.plainText: Here shall they make their ransom on the sand

lines.plainText: Or with their blood stain this discoloured shore

lines.plainText: And thou that art his mate make boot of this

lines.text: What is my ransom, master? Let me know.

lines.text: A thousand crowns, or else lay down your head.
lines.plainText: A thousand crowns or else lay down your head

lines.text: And so much shall you give, or off goes yours.
lines.plainText: And so much shall you give or off goes yours

lines.text: What, think you much to pay two thousand crowns,
lines.plainText: What think you much to pay two thousand crowns

lines.text: And bear the name and port of gentlemen?
lines.plainText: And bear the name and port of gentlemen

lines.text: Cut both the villains' throats—for die you shall.
lines.plainText: Cut both the villains' throatsfor die you shall

lines.plainText: The lives of those which we have lost in fight

lines.text: Be counterpoised with such a petty sum!
lines.plainText: Be counterpoised with such a petty sum

lines.text: I'll give it, sir, and therefore spare my life.
lines.plainText: I'll give it sir and therefore spare my life

lines.text: And so will I, and write home for it straight.
lines.plainText: And so will I and write home for it straight

lines.text: [To Suffolk.] I lost mine eye in laying the prize aboard,
lines.plainText: To Suffolk I lost mine eye in laying the prize aboard

lines.text: And therefore to revenge it shalt thou die;
lines.plainText: And therefore to revenge it shalt thou die

lines.text: And so should these, if I might have my will.
lines.plainText: And so should these if I might have my will

lines.text: Be not so rash; take ransom, let him live.
lines.plainText: Be not so rash take ransom let him live

lines.text: Look on my George; I am a gentleman.
lines.plainText: Look on my George I am a gentleman

lines.text: Rate me at what thou wilt, thou shalt be paid.
lines.plainText: Rate me at what thou wilt thou shalt be paid

lines.text: And so am I; my name is Walter Whitmore.
lines.plainText: And so am I my name is Walter Whitmore

lines.text: How now! Why starts thou? What, doth death affright?

lines.plainText: Thy name affrights me in whose sound is death

lines.text: A cunning man did calculate my birth
lines.plainText: A cunning man did calculate my birth

lines.plainText: And told me that by water I should die

lines.text: Yet let not this make thee be bloody-minded;
lines.plainText: Yet let not this make thee be bloodyminded

lines.plainText: Never yet did base dishonour blur our name

lines.plainText: But with our sword we wiped away the blot

lines.plainText: Therefore when merchantlike I sell revenge

lines.plainText: Broke be my sword my arms torn and defaced

lines.plainText: And I proclaimed a coward through the world

lines.text: The Duke of Suffolk, muffled up in rags?
lines.plainText: The Duke of Suffolk muffled up in rags

lines.plainText: Ay but these rags are no part of the Duke

lines.plainText: Jove sometime went disguised and why not I

lines.plainText: But Jove was never slain as thou shalt be

lines.plainText: The honourable blood of Lancaster

lines.plainText: Must not be shed by such a jaded groom

lines.plainText: Hast thou not kissed thy hand and held my stirrup

lines.plainText: Bareheaded plodded by my footcloth mule

lines.plainText: And thought thee happy when I shook my head

lines.plainText: And duly waited for my coming forth

lines.plainText: And therefore shall it charm thy riotous tongue

lines.plainText: Speak captain shall I stab the forlorn swain

lines.plainText: Convey him hence and on our longboat's side

lines.plainText: Troubles the silver spring where England drinks

lines.plainText: Now will I dam up this thy yawning mouth

lines.text: For swallowing the treasure of the realm.
lines.plainText: For swallowing the treasure of the realm

lines.plainText: Thy lips that kissed the Queen shall sweep the ground

lines.plainText: And thou that smiledst at good Duke Humphrey's death

lines.plainText: For daring to affy a mighty lord

lines.plainText: Unto the daughter of a worthless king

lines.plainText: By devilish policy art thou grown great

lines.plainText: Disdain to call us lord and Picardy
